title: There is a keyboard remapping that doesn´t work
author: DgBodego

status.label: AltGr punctuation remap needs verification
status.detail: Screenshots show Alt (Left)+grave to { working and Alt (Left)+plus to } failing, while the report says AltGr on a Spanish layout. Current main has explicit AltGr handling, but capture/runtime key identity is not verified.

next_action: Confirm the active keyboard layout, exact physical chord including Shift, and behavior on a current build; compare the two source events using the reproduction steps.

judgment.rationale: The issue supplies an asymmetric reproduction and screenshots: the grave-key mapping produces {, but the plus-key mapping does not. The screenshot records the source modifier as Alt (Left), whereas the report describes AltGr on a Spanish layout; current upstream main explicitly recognizes AltGr as right Alt with left Ctrl and has regression tests for that path. This makes an editor/runtime representation mismatch for a layout-dependent OEM punctuation key a testable, low-confidence hypothesis.
evidence: The report describes an English keyboard setup with Spanish keyboard distribution and says AltGr+grave maps to { successfully while AltGr+plus is unresponsive.
The screenshots show saved mappings Alt (Left)+grave to { and Alt (Left)+plus to }; Notepad shows the first working and the second producing no character.
The report lists PowerToys 0.91.1 and Windows 11 Pro 24H2 build 26100.4061. No comments, assignees, or linked fix are present.

At upstream main 8cfe69247aef8aabadeeafbdafaecab293a2a7f3, KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp:669-679 detects AltGr as VK_RMENU while VK_LCONTROL is down, and OSLevelShortcutRemappingTests.cpp:2374 onward covers AltGr state handling. This confirms the code path exists but does not prove it handles this captured OEM key sequence.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce both saved mappings on a current build with the Spanish keyboard layout, record the exact key events and stored source shortcut, then correct capture/runtime normalization only if the plus-key path differs.

fix_assessment.rationale: A targeted AltGr/OEM-key normalization change may be warranted if the editor and runtime represent the Spanish-layout plus chord differently. Current evidence supports investigation, not a confirmed implementation; the screenshot/prose modifier mismatch and old PowerToys version are the material uncertainties.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve AltGr identity for layout-dependent punctuation shortcuts
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The saved screenshot records Alt (Left) for both shortcuts, while the report says the physical modifier is AltGr. Current main identifies AltGr from the VK_LCONTROL+VK_RMENU event pair. The failing plus chord may also use a different physical OEM key or Shift state than the shortcut editor saved, causing a capture/runtime match mismatch; this hypothesis is unconfirmed.
plan: Reproduce both screenshot mappings on a current build with the active Spanish keyboard layout and confirm the physical key sequence for plus, including Shift.

Trace editor-captured source key/modifier data and runtime events for the working grave key and failing plus key; compare VK_LCONTROL, VK_RMENU, VK_OEM_PLUS, Shift, and the stored Shortcut representation.

If the editor and runtime disagree about the AltGr or OEM-plus representation, normalize capture and matching so both use the same physical chord while preserving the distinction between left Alt and AltGr where required.
Add regression coverage for AltGr+grave and AltGr+plus on the Spanish layout, including required Shift state, and verify ordinary Alt shortcuts remain unchanged.
verification: On the reported Windows 11 24H2 setup, both saved mappings produce { and } in Notepad when their corresponding AltGr chords are pressed.
Focused tests cover the captured source modifier and OEM-key sequence for both mappings, including key-up cleanup and any required Shift state.
Existing ordinary left-Alt shortcuts and AltGr state tests continue to pass.

confidence.rationale: The screenshots and report disagree on whether the source is left Alt or AltGr, and the failing plus key may be layout- or Shift-dependent. Current main has AltGr-specific handling, but no current-build reproduction or exact event trace establishes a defect in that path.

issue_context.summary: On a Spanish keyboard layout, the reporter says an AltGr+grave mapping outputs { but an AltGr+plus mapping intended to output } does nothing.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.91.1 and Windows 11 Pro 24H2 build 26100.4061.
The reporter says the keyboard setup is English with a Spanish keyboard distribution.
The attached Keyboard Manager screenshot shows Alt (Left)+grave to { and Alt (Left)+plus to }; a Notepad screenshot shows the first mapping working and the second producing no character.
Current upstream main 8cfe69247aef8aabadeeafbdafaecab293a2a7f3 recognizes AltGr when right Alt is pressed while left Ctrl is down and contains AltGr shortcut-state tests.
inferences: The displayed Alt (Left) source may not represent the reported physical AltGr event, or the reporter may be using a different modifier than the screenshot suggests.
The Spanish-layout plus key may depend on a different physical OEM key or Shift state than the shortcut editor saved; this remains unconfirmed.
A capture/runtime key identity mismatch is plausible but cannot be inferred from the screenshots alone.
issue_context.analysis: The asymmetric result and screenshots are enough for a maintainer to attempt the reported sequence, but they do not establish the precise chord: the prose says AltGr while the UI shows Alt (Left), and plus may be a shifted/layout-dependent key. Current main has explicit AltGr recognition, so compare captured shortcut data with runtime events before any code change.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body and all screenshots, including the saved source/target rows and observed Notepad output; no comments or assignees exist.
Checked upstream main at 8cfe69247aef8aabadeeafbdafaecab293a2a7f3: KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp:669-679 recognizes the VK_LCONTROL+VK_RMENU AltGr sequence; key-up handling is at 994-1007.
Checked OSLevelShortcutRemappingTests.cpp:2374 onward; current tests cover AltGr state reset but not the reported Spanish-layout punctuation mappings.
No linked fix or direct duplicate was established.

information_gaps.information: The exact active Windows keyboard-layout name and the physical keys used for each mapping, including whether Shift is held for plus; confirm whether failure persists on PowerToys 0.100.2 or newer.
